definitions.explanation: Relating to the public sphere, government, or matters open to general knowledge. Contrasts with private or unofficial matters.

examples.japanese: {公|おおやけ}の{場|ば}で{発言|はつげん}する。
その{情報|じょうほう}はまだ{公|おおやけ}にされていない。
examples.english: That information has not been made public yet.

examples.japanese: {私的|してき}な{問題|もんだい}を{公|おおやけ}にするべきではないと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I don't think private matters should be made public.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{公|おおやけ}にする (make public, disclose)
・{公|おおやけ}になる (become public, come to light)
・{公|おおやけ}の{場|ば} (public setting, official venue)
・{公|おおやけ}の{立場|たちば} (official position)

USAGE NOTES:
The やまと{言葉|ことば} (native Japanese word) for "public," contrasting with the sino-Japanese {公|こう} used in compounds like {公共|こうきょう} (public), {公式|こうしき} (official). {公|おおやけ}にする means "to make public" or "to disclose," while {公|おおやけ}になる means "to become publicly known." The word implies visibility to society at large and often carries a sense of formality or officialness.
